summary: This bill amends IRC section 7508A to let the IRS postpone federal tax deadlines for state-declared natural disasters when requested by a governor (after FEMA consultation) and extends the maximum mandatory postponement period from 60 to 120 days.

scores.thoughts: The bill amends IRC rules on postponing tax deadlines for disasters but contains no provisions related to government expenditures, appropriations, or spending levels. It is purely administrative relief for taxpayers.

The bill directly modifies Section 7508A of the Internal Revenue Code to expand the Secretary's authority to grant filing and payment extensions for state-declared disasters and lengthens mandatory extensions from 60 to 120 days. This provides tangible taxpayer relief in the form of deferred deadlines, which aligns with reducing the immediate tax burden.
